data.title: Si Her Collective Capital
data.description: Join Kara Howard, Co-Founder and Ecosystem Lead, for the Si Her DeFi kickoff on collective capital and DeFi capital models.
aboutText: This opening session introduces the Si Her DeFi cohort and explores how collective capital models can support community-led funding. Kara Howard guides the discussion and sets the foundation for the learning journey ahead.

data.title: From TradFi to DeFi
data.description: Kara Howard maps the move from traditional finance into decentralized markets and new forms of access.
aboutText: Explore how traditional finance and decentralized finance differ, what changes when financial services use blockchain-based tools, and how these models may affect access. Kara Howard guides this Si Her DeFi session through the key concepts and practical questions to consider before participating.

data.title: Token Fundamentals
data.description: This session views tokens not as investment, but as purpose-built economic tools and financial instruments.
aboutText: Explore tokens as tools for participation, incentives, and coordination. Diana Ilieva, tokenomics consultant at FinDaS.org, introduces the fundamentals of how token design supports a community or product.

speakers.name: Diana Ilieva
speakers.bio: Diana is a tokenomics consultant at FinDaS Ltd with over 5 years of experience in creating data-driven token economy models for various crypto projects. Diana has created the tokenomics for P2E projects, stablecoins, lending & DeFi protocols, RWA and consulted on narrow topics like DAO structures and processes.
speakers.sessionDescription: This sessions views tokens not as investment, but as purpose-built economic tools and financial instruments. We'll discuss issuance, value drivers, release schedules and when a token has strong fundamentals.

data.title: Stable(coin) Confidence
data.description: Esther Wong introduces stablecoins and how they can support accessible, everyday digital payments.
aboutText: Learn what stablecoins are, how they differ from more volatile crypto assets, and where they fit in real payment experiences. Esther Wong is CEO and Co-Founder of Cashi.

speakers.name: Esther Wong
speakers.bio: Esther Wong is the Founder and CEO of Cashi, a global spending card built to make digital dollars simple, usable and borderless. Before founding Cashi, she spent seven years at Crypto.com, where she helped build and scale its card program into one of the largest in the industry. With deep experience across cards, payments and consumer financial products, Esther is focused on making global money easier to hold, send and spend for everyday users.
speakers.sessionDescription: Stablecoin Confidence is a practical masterclass designed to make stablecoins feel simple, useful and approachable. Esther will break down what stablecoins are, why they matter for people earning, saving and spending globally, and how to use them with more confidence in everyday life.

data.title: What the Infra?
data.description: Jennifer Kim explores the infrastructure that makes decentralized finance usable and connected.
aboutText: A practical introduction to the systems beneath DeFi and how infrastructure supports access, interoperability, and everyday use. Jennifer Kim is Head of Business Development at SODAX.

data.title: Decentralized Futures
data.description: Ramona Tudorancea explores how decentralized technology could shape future products, communities, and participation.
aboutText: Consider emerging decentralized models and the choices that affect who can build, participate, and benefit. Ramona Tudorancea is Co-Founder and Partner at IXIAN.

speakers.name: Ramona Tudorancea
speakers.bio: Ramona comes from a legal background of international corporate and finance, investment funds and M&A, and brings legal strategy and multi-jurisdictional structuring to a new level, with a focus on the Law of the Network State, the evolution of organizations and RWAs tokenization. She is also a Graduate (GradCG) of the Chartered Governance Institute UK and Ireland.
speakers.sessionDescription:
Decentralized Futures explores how decentralized technologies are evolving beyond financial protocols into new infrastructure for coordination, governance, ownership, and institution-building. Drawing from legal engineering, Web3, Network State, and emerging models of digital organization, Ramona Tudorancea examines what it takes to turn decentralization from an ideology into durable real-world systems.

Beyond DeFi: Explore how decentralized infrastructure can reshape organizations, communities, governance, and economic coordination.
From Protocols to Institutions: Examine how code, law, governance, and incentives can work together.
New Models of Ownership & Participation: Consider emerging approaches to contribution, digital property, community capital, and shared value creation.
Designing Decentralized Futures: Investigate the opportunities and challenges of building systems that preserve individual agency while remaining legally resilient, economically viable, and capable of operating in the real world.

data.title: Si Her Trade
data.description: Karin Kusano introduces Si Her Trade and ways to think about access and participation in digital asset markets.
aboutText: Explore the role of capital formation and trade in the broader DeFi ecosystem with Karin Kusano, Director of Capital Formation at CryptoMommi.
